speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and whether they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions firm and dome-shaped, with a central dimple or umbilication? Have you noticed any spread to the face or extremities, or any recent fever or respiratory symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of pearly, umbilicated papules in a daycare-attending toddler is classic for Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
